newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on EPA rate comment report.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends down on EPA rate comment report.

text.p: The benchmark March three-month Euroyen futures contract sank to a lower settlement in Tokyo on Monday, after a report quoting a Japanese official as saying that a rise in the official discount rate is very possible by the end of this year.
The report set off heavy sales of Japanese government bonds (JGBs) and briefly dragged Euroyen futures as low as 99.15. Earlier in the day, March Euroyen touched a high of 99.21.
Volume for the day was 67,128 contracts.

Economic Planning Agency (EPA) Minister Taro Aso, asked in an interview in New York with Dow Jones news agency about the possibility that Japan's official discount rate could rise by the end of the year, was quoted as replying: "It should be higher than now; it's very possible. That's all I can say at this moment." Asked why the official discount rate might have risen by then, Aso was quoted as saying: "The economy will have grown by then."
In the interview, Aso also emphasized that any decision on the official discount rate is up to the Bank of Japan (BOJ).
The key September JGB contract was last traded at 126.47, down from Friday's close of 126.67.

"Although this report has had an impact on the market, you have to wonder how they would actually manage to carry off a rate rise now. After all, the outlook for smaller and medium-sized firms is still not so good and there are other difficulties suggesting the economy is not making all that much progress," one city bank trader said.
He added that support held at 99.15 despite Aso's quoted comments, suggesting that Euroyen futures still retained some of their recent fundamental firmness.

Another city bank trader said, however, that further sales could still ensue on technical factors due to the March contract's settlement below 99.19 today, adding that the market was a bit wary of possible overseas selling.
Earlier in the day, Euroyen futures had been buoyed by weaker Nikkei stocks, with March Euroyen inching close to its contract high of 99.22.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 400 billion yen into the money market this morning, against a projected fund shortfall of 120 billion yen.
The weighted average of the key overnight call rate was likely to be 0.50 percent on Monday, unchanged from Friday, traders said.
The continued firmness in the key overnight call rate was due to strong fund demand from the private sector for tax payments to the government, traders said.

About 60 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) was issued at 0.63 percent on Monday. About 30 billion yen worth of two-month CDs was issued at 0.64 percent and about 100 billion yen worth of one-month CDs was issued at 0.56 percent. All CD rates were flat from Friday.
